title: Superweight Damage Repair in OLMo-1B utilizing a Single Row Patch (CPU-only Experiment)
primary_claim: Ablating a single 'superweight' in OLMo-1B causes perplexity to spike from 17.4 to 2884.3 with pathological outputs, but training a single trainable row-vector patch via KL distillation from the original model recovers approximately 93% of the lost performance while learning a new, largely orthogonal distributed direction rather than relearning the original weight (cosine similarity to the original row ~0.13).
quote: Surprisingly, it worked! Perplexity dropped drastically(i.e 2884.3 to 25.2) nearing the original model's values, and the Tokyo prompt was fixed... I observed approximately 93% recovery.
tolerance_rationale: headline is a compound of 4 numbers; compare the components by hand
inspector_notes: Extremely reproducible: results/07_compare_results.txt already committed in the repo contains the exact target numbers (PPL 17.41->2884.33->25.24, cos(base,delta)=0.1336), i.e. the repo's own prior run reproduces the post's headline claim verbatim. Ungated model, all-CPU by design, trivial compute.
headline_artifact: results/07_compare_results.txt and results.png — BASE/BROKEN/PATCHED NLL/PPL table plus cosine-similarity stats for delta_row vs base_row, produced by 07_compare_patch.py
